title: Rajendra's two theories
body: Rajendra paced the room and explained Professor Gaitonde's experience with two theories. First, catastrophe theory: in a face-to-face war on open ground between armies of comparable strength and armour, much depends on leadership and morale. At Panipat the Maratha and Abdali forces were evenly matched. When Vishwasrao, heir to the Peshwa, was killed and Bhausaheb rushed into the melee and was never seen again, the troops lost their fighting spirit and an utter rout followed. On the torn page the bullet missed Vishwasrao; the event, taken as an omen, boosted morale and turned the tide. Second, quantum theory: the behaviour of an electron cannot be predicted definitively, only as odds, so one may imagine many worlds, each with the electron in a different place. Just as an electron can jump between energy states, Rajendra suggested the professor had made a transition to another world and back. He had not travelled to the past or the future; he had been in the present, experiencing a world whose history had branched off at Panipat.
